key_insight: The paper shows that topology optimization can be extended to high-temperature components by directly optimizing against nonlinear creep deformation instead of only elastic stiffness.
engineering_relevance: This enables safer, longer-life designs for metallic parts such as turbine blades operating under sustained thermal and mechanical loads.
method: Uses a differentiable thermo-structural topology optimization framework with the Norton creep model.
Solves transient creep response with backward Euler over the service life and uses JAX automatic differentiation for adjoint sensitivities.
Supports gradient-based optimization for 2D benchmarks and a 3D graded-material turbine blade design challenge.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports benchmark studies showing substantially lower permanent deformation than elastic-stiffness-only designs, plus a 3D turbine blade challenge demonstrating the framework under coupled thermal, nonlinear, and multi-material conditions.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate creep constitutive parameters and a differentiable transient solver, so results may be sensitive to material-model calibration and computational cost.
paper_title: Thermo-Structural Topology Optimization Considering Nonlinear Creep
